sections.title: Market Pulse: A Resilient Close to a Volatile July

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Rally to Close July, Fueled by Tech Earnings Amid Inflation Concerns
items.summary: U.S. equities concluded a volatile July with a rally on Friday, July 31, 2026, driven by strong performances from major technology companies like Amazon and Microsoft. The S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and Nasdaq Composite all posted gains, despite persistent worries about inflation and climbing Treasury yields. The market exhibited a concentrated nature, with a handful of mega-cap stocks accounting for the majority of the S&P 500's positive movement.

sections.title: Top Movers: Notable Stocks on July 31, 2026

items.headline: Amazon Soars on Strong Q2 Profit and AWS Growth
items.summary: Amazon ($AMZN) surged after reporting stronger-than-expected second-quarter profits, suggesting that its significant AI investments are yielding positive returns. The company's AWS segment showed robust growth, contributing to investor optimism.

items.headline: Microsoft Rises on Robust Earnings and Azure Performance
items.summary: Microsoft ($MSFT) gained following its robust quarterly results, which highlighted strong performance in its Azure cloud business and exceeded sales and cloud growth forecasts.

items.headline: Alphabet Climbs Higher
items.summary: Alphabet ($GOOGL) posted a significant gain, contributing to the overall positive sentiment in the technology sector.

items.headline: Apple Drops on Lackluster Revenue Forecast
items.summary: Apple ($AAPL) experienced a notable decline after issuing a lackluster forecast for upcoming revenue growth. Investor concerns were also fueled by rising component costs, linked to the broader AI hardware boom, and slowing growth in key segments, including its Services business.

items.headline: Reddit Shares Crater
items.summary: Reddit ($RDDT) saw a significant drop in its share price.

items.headline: Micron Technology Falls
items.summary: Micron Technology ($MU) declined amidst broader weakness in the semiconductor industry.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady Amidst Inflationary Concerns
items.summary: The Federal Reserve maintained interest rates at 3.50-3.75% during its latest meeting, though the decision was not unanimous, with three members dissenting in favor of a rate hike. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the committee's commitment to addressing persistent inflation, as Treasury yields continued to climb with the 10-year yield reaching 4.7% and the 30-year climbing above 5.22%.

items.headline: Q2 GDP Cools, Jobless Claims Tick Up
items.summary: The U.S. economy's second-quarter GDP growth cooled to 1.5%, missing consensus estimates of a 2.0% expansion, primarily due to a surge in imports. Meanwhile, jobless claims for the week ending July 25 increased by 9,000 to 197,000, while continuing claims saw a decrease.

items.headline: Consumer Discretionary Leads, Materials Lagging in Sector Performance
items.summary: On Friday, the Consumer Discretionary sector was the top performer, gaining 6.07%, propelled by strong tech earnings. In contrast, the Materials sector was the worst-performing, falling 2.71%, with stocks like Corteva ($CTVA) and Linde ($LIN) experiencing significant drops due to missed revenue estimates and declining operating margins, respectively.

items.headline: Major Oil Companies Report Strong Earnings
items.summary: ExxonMobil ($XOM) announced robust second-quarter 2026 earnings of $14.5 billion, or $3.48 per share, with adjusted earnings reaching $14.7 billion. Shell and Chevron were also expected to report high profits for the quarter, benefiting from elevated crude prices.

items.headline: AbbVie Posts Strong Q2, Announces Acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics
items.summary: AbbVie ($ABBV) reported strong second-quarter 2026 financial results, with adjusted diluted EPS of $3.65. The pharmaceutical giant also announced a proposed acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics, aimed at strengthening its immunology leadership.
